# CONSULTATION REPORT — ENDOCRINOLOGY

Patient : **JACKSON, Teresa**

DOB : **1960-03-16 (64 y)**

Health ins. no. : **JACT 6053 1692**

File no. : **88-48452**

Date of visit : **2024-09-06**

Referring MD : **Dr Brittany Lewis**

Dictation ID: 457648
Unit: GMF

## Reason for consultation

Poorly controlled type 2 diabetes, endocrinology consultation.

## History of present illness

This 64-year-old woman has had type 2 diabetes for 11 years. HbA1c has risen from 7.4% to 9.1% over the past year despite metformin and gliclazide at maximal doses.

She reports polyuria and nocturia x2, fatigue and a 4 kg weight gain. Home glucose readings range from 9 to 14 mmol/L fasting.

## Past medical history

- Type 2 diabetes (2013)
- Hypertension
- Obesity (BMI 34)
- Hypothyroidism

## Current medications

- Metformin 1000 mg PO BID

- Gliclazide MR 120 mg PO daily

- Perindopril 8 mg PO daily

- Levothyroxine 88 mcg PO daily

- Rosuvastatin 10 mg PO daily

## Allergies

No known drug allergies.

## Physical examination

**BP** 159/70 mmHg | **HR** 83 /min | **RR** 18 /min | **Temp** 36.7 °C | **SpO2** 99 % RA | **Weight** 60.6 kg | **Height** 184 cm | **BMI** 33.8

BMI 34.2. Blood pressure 146/88. Fundoscopy deferred. Monofilament testing: reduced sensation at 2 sites on the left foot. Pedal pulses present. No ulcers.

## Impression

1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia (E11.65)
2. Diabetic polyneuropathy (E11.42)
3. Obesity, class I (E66.01)

## Plan

1. Start semaglutide 0.25 mg SC weekly, titrate to 1 mg over 8 weeks.
2. Continue metformin; reduce gliclazide to 60 mg to limit hypoglycemia.
3. Labs: HbA1c, creatinine, urine ACR, lipid panel in 3 months.
4. Refer to ophthalmology and foot-care nursing.
5. Diabetes education program referral; follow-up in 3 months.

Dr Kevin Schwartz, Endocrinology
